requirement: Tracker row 0.11 — build the CombatDirector, CutsceneDirector and TransitionDirector autoloads (Doc 00 §2.3, §7.4, §8), register them above RuntimeDirector, wire the resolver stubs that name row 0.11, and prove the row's Verify column plus Doc 00 §12 checks 23 and 28 in tests/test_all.gd.
priorState: Rows 0.1-0.10 Done. Suite green at 253 checks. RuntimeDirector exists and is pure; it reaches other systems through two nullable handles (player, zone_manager) and carries six `ponytail:` comments naming row 0.11.

toolchain.gate: Exit 0 is NOT sufficient — Godot exits 0 when test_all.gd fails to parse. Green means the run also printed `test_all: N checks passed` with N greater than the previous row's count and zero FAIL lines.

architecture.decision: Three separate autoloads as Doc 00 §2.2's table declares, registered immediately above RuntimeDirector. Every gameplay mutation stays inside RuntimeDirector._resolve(); the three directors own only their own domain state. Cutscene completion is POLLED by the resolver at priority 6 rather than signalled back, so no new RuntimeEvent.Type value is added and no autoload writes player state.
alternatives: Fold all three into RuntimeDirector now (tracker D18). Rejected: D18 is explicitly deferred until after P6, and the resolver's purity contract (no tween, no await, no Input) forbids TransitionDirector's overlay tween living in that file.

Add a CUTSCENE_COMPLETE value to RuntimeEvent.Type and have CutsceneDirector publish it. Rejected: amends Doc 00 §2.5's authored enum for one internal handoff, and the enum's comment says a rename or reorder is a silent breakage.

CutsceneDirector emits `finished` and RuntimeDirector commits from the signal handler. Rejected: a gameplay commit outside _resolve() breaks the §4.1 tick contract and cannot be stepped by the §12 harness.
seams: S1 — project.godot registration order: CombatDirector, CutsceneDirector, TransitionDirector all go ABOVE RuntimeDirector. The AudioDirector, ZoneManager and SessionDirector slots in §2.2's table stay empty until rows 3.2, 2.3 and 0.12.

S2 — §14.1 holds: only RuntimeDirector mutates gameplay state. CombatDirector owns threat/boss/aggro (its own domain), CutsceneDirector owns the queue and the active config, TransitionDirector owns pixels and nothing else. None of the three writes player.state, GameState, or Weirdness.

S3 — CutsceneDirector.take_finished() is the handoff. The resolver polls it at priority 6, then writes on_complete_flag, returns the player to FREE, and enqueues on_complete_intent so it resolves next tick through its own priority row (§8.2.1).

S4 — CutsceneDirector.request() validates and enqueues CUTSCENE_REQUEST; the resolver remains the acceptor, preserving §8.1 steps 1-2. request() rejects an on_complete_intent outside the three permitted types AT REQUEST TIME (§12 check 23).

S5 — every duration in the three directors is a physics-tick count derived from a float constant (§2.4). TransitionDirector is the one place a tween is legal, because it is presentation only, and it must expose no method that reads or writes gameplay state.

S6 — CombatDirector.THREAT_LINGER is Doc 4 §2.7's IDLE_HIDE_DELAY. HudVisibility does not exist (tracker D9), so the float is inlined here with a guard check that fires the day row 3.5 creates the class with a different value.
architecture.note: The doc constrains this design heavily — §2.2 names three autoloads, §14.1 names the one committer — so the only genuinely open fork was the completion handoff, settled above rather than in a full ADR.

tasks.result: autoload/cutscene_director.gd added and registered between CombatDirector and RuntimeDirector; suite green at 339 checks (was 297). deviations: Doc 00 §8.1 step 5 says CutsceneDirector sets the player to CUTSCENE. That is the direct mutation §8.4 deletes DialogueLine.pause_player for, and §14.1 forbids. Doc 00 §8 defines no completion path at all — no event type, no signal, no method — yet §8.2.1 requires the resolver to write on_complete_flag and enqueue on_complete_intent on completion. Filled by seam S3's polled complete()/take_completed() pair. §8 should name it.

Doc 00 §7.7 assigns the 0.15 s arrival wait to CutsceneDirector, but RuntimeDirector already owns ARRIVAL_GRACE_TICKS and counts it in _tick_durations(). Enforcing it in the director would be a second counter (§0.1, §2.4) and a gameplay gate outside the resolver (§14.1). Built as the marker half only; the resolver's half is T4.

deviations: Doc 00 §8.1 step 6 has no completion sentinel: CutsceneDirector.take_completed() returns {} for `nothing finished`, which is indistinguishable from a cutscene authored with an empty config. The resolver's poll is therefore two-armed — a non-empty handoff, OR the player sitting in CUTSCENE while the director holds nothing active. Giving the director a `has_completed()` would let the second arm go; deliberately not done, because editing a verified file was out of this task's scope.

Doc 00 §8.1 step 6 says a completion returns the player to FREE, and §4.2 row 4 lets damage commit at priority 4 on that same tick, leaving the player already HURT. Forcing FREE would erase the hit, so the return is guarded on `state == CUTSCENE` and row 4.1's recovery returns control in that case. The doc names neither the conflict nor the resolution.

Doc 00 §7.4 step 9 and §11.2 step 9 imply an arrival story may be requested during a transition, but §6.3 and §11.1 discard anything published behind an opaque overlay, so `_defer_survivors()` drops it rather than deferring it. §7.7's grace therefore only ever refuses a request authored AFTER release. The step ordering implies this and never states it.

Doc 00 §11.2 step 5 lumps the combat reset and the ordinary-enemy respawn into one step, so the step is now half-delivered. The `ponytail:` comment splits it: combat is row 0.11's and landed, enemies are row 2.7's.
